topic: Proof of Snell's Law: The Principle of Least Time

outline.topic: Proof of Snell's Law: The Principle of Least Time

sections.title: Introduction: The Lifeguard Dilemma (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Use a visual analogy: A lifeguard on the beach needs to reach a drowning swimmer in the water. Running on sand is faster than swimming. Should they run in a straight line, or aim for a point that minimizes total time?
sections.example: An animation showing a lifeguard choosing between a straight path (shorter distance, slower speed) vs. a refracted path (longer distance, higher speed).

sections.title: Prerequisite: Fermat’s Principle (0:45-1:30)
sections.content: Introduce Fermat's Principle of Least Time: Light travels between two points along the path that takes the least amount of time. Define v1 = c/n1 and v2 = c/n2 (velocity in two media).
sections.example: A graphic showing the wavefronts changing speed at the interface, demonstrating that 'shortest path' in time $\neq$ 'shortest path' in distance.

sections.title: Mathematical Modeling (1:30-3:00)
sections.content: Set up a coordinate system at the interface. Define point A (0, h1) and point B (x, -h2). Let the refracted point be (y, 0). Express Total Time T(y) = sqrt(h1^2 + y^2)/v1 + sqrt(h2^2 + (x-y)^2)/v2.
sections.example: An interactive diagram where moving point (y, 0) dynamically updates the calculated Time T graph, highlighting the global minimum.

sections.title: Derivation: The Calculus of Refraction (3:00-4:15)
sections.content: Take the derivative dT/dy and set it to zero. Using the geometric definition of sine (sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse), show that dT/dy = sin(θ1)/v1 - sin(θ2)/v2 = 0.
sections.example: Side-by-side split screen: Left shows the geometric triangle at the interface; Right shows the algebraic steps resulting in (sin θ1)/v1 = (sin θ2)/v2.

sections.title: Synthesis & Snell's Law (4:15-5:00)
sections.content: Substitute v = c/n into the result to reach n1 sin(θ1) = n2 sin(θ2). Summarize that light's 'intelligence' is actually just nature optimizing for time.
sections.example: A final visual of a laser beam passing through a glass block, with labels showing how the refractive indices directly dictate the bending angles proven by the math.

animations: 1. Fade in sand (yellow #FFD700) and water (blue #0000FF). Lifeguard [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lifeguard.svg] at point A, Swimmer [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/swimmer.svg] at point B.
2. Animate lifeguard [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lifeguard.svg] running along sand (fast, green path #00FF00).
3. Animate direct straight line to swimmer [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/swimmer.svg] (slow, red path #FF0000).
4. Animate refracted path: running, then swimming (optimal path, orange #FFA500).

5. Highlight the optimal path (orange #FFA500) and compare time between lifeguard [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lifeguard.svg] and swimmer [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/swimmer.svg].

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: Fermat’s Principle (0:45-1:30)
lecture_lines: Light follows path of least time.
animations: 1. Show light rays (white #FFFFFF) traveling between two points originating from a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/flashlight.svg].
2. Highlight light path (green #00FF00) as the fastest time path passing through a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/glass.svg].
3. Introduce refractive index symbols (n1, n2) near media labels.

storyboard.title: Mathematical Modeling (1:30-3:00)
animations: 1. Draw x-axis and y-axis using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/interface.svg]. Label origin (0,0) (white #FFFFFF).
2. Place point A (above) and point B (below) at fixed coordinates using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/coordinate.svg].
3. Draw line from A to interface, then to B. Label variable distance x (yellow #FFD700).
4. Graph the total time function T(x) on a side plot using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/graph.svg] (white #FFFFFF).
5. Mark minimum of T(x) curve and relate to optimal path geometry using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/points.svg] (orange #FFA500).

storyboard.title: Derivation: The Calculus of Refraction (3:00-4:15)
lecture_lines: Differentiate time with respect to distance.
animations: 1. Display total time equation T(x) (white #FFFFFF).
2. Animate derivative symbol d/dx (yellow #FFD700).
3. Show equation terms simplifying to Snell's law form.
4. Highlight ratio sin(θ1)/sin(θ2) (blue #0000FF) and v1/v2 (green #00FF00).
5. Final visual proof showing geometric relationship (white #FFFFFF).

storyboard.title: Synthesis & Snell's Law (4:15-5:00)
animations: 1. Write v = c/n for both media [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/light.svg] (white #FFFFFF).
2. Substitute velocities into the sine ratio equation.
3. Display final Snell's Law: n1*sin(θ1) = n2*sin(θ2) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/light.svg] (bold green #00FF00).
